chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Hisham al-Kindi, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Beware of doing a deed by which they would reproach us, for the child of the bad [character] shames his father with his deed. Be an adornment for the one to whom you have attached yourselves, and do not be a disgrace upon him. Pray among their clans, visit their sick, and attend their funerals. And do not let them precede you to any good, for you are more deserving of it than they. And by Allah, Allah was not worshipped with anything more beloved to Him than Al-Khab.' I said, 'And what is Al-Khab?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'Al-Taqiyya (dissimulation).'
ai.seo_question: What is the definition of Al-Khab in Shia theology and how does Taqiyya relate to worship?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes Taqiyya not merely as a defensive mechanism but as a proactive virtue of 'Al-Khab' (concealment) that serves as the most beloved form of worship to Allah. It emphasizes social integration—praying with, visiting, and attending the funerals of the general community—to ensure the Shia are an 'adornment' rather than a 'disgrace' to the Imams, thereby preventing opponents from using their practices as a pretext for criticism.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Hisham Al Kindy who said,

‘I heard Abu Abdullahasws saying: ‘Beware of doing a deed weasws would be faulted with, for the evil child shames his father with his deed. Become an adornment for the one you cut yourselves off to and do not become a disgrace upon him. Help out among their clan, and console their sick ones, and attend their funerals, and do not let them precede you to the goodness, for you all are closer with it than them, and Allahazwj has not been worshipped with anything more Beloved to Himazwj that Al-Khab’. I said, ‘And what is Al-Khab?’ Heasws said: ‘The dissimulation (Taqiyya)’.
en.sarwar: 11. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Hisham al-Kindy who has said the following:

“I heard abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) saying, ‘You must never do anything that may embarrass us. A small boy causes embarrassment to his father because of his misdeeds. Be the beauty for those to whom you are devoted and do not be an embarrassment to them. Pray along with their tribes, visit their people in ill health, attend their funerals and do not allow anyone exceed you in good deeds. You have all the more reason to exceed others in good deeds. By Allah, no worship is more beloved to Allah than worshipping Him in (al- Khab’).’ I then asked, ‘What is al-Khab’?’ The Imam said, ‘It is al-Taqiyyah.”’
